title: The Light of New York

description.main: Black-and-white photographs of New York streets at dawn by Jean-Michel Berts.
description.extended:
Black-and-white photographs of New York streets at dawn by the French photographer Jean-Michel Berts, published by Assouline in 2007.

The publisher describes the city at that hour as muted, subdued and mysterious, caught in moments of dream-like serenity. The book is a hardcover of 128 pages.

Berts has photographed cities in black and white for more than 30 years. He says his series of city books began with a trip to Venice in 2001 and also covers Paris, London, Tokyo, Jerusalem and Istanbul, and he names Ansel Adams, Edward Weston and Karl Hugo Schmölz as influences. In his view, leaving people out of the frame lets human achievements speak for themselves.
